{"body":"## Problem

Agent and Conductor workspaces have no `.venv`. Nothing creates one: `.conductor/settings.toml` has only a `[prompts]` section and no setup script. Without a venv, pyright cannot resolve third-party imports (`reflex`, etc.). This surfaced during #347, where I could check only `reportUnknownMemberType` and had to leave the rest unverified.

A full local pyright run was also killed (exit 137, probably out of memory) on an ~8 GB sandbox. So syncing the venv locally would fix import resolution but may not make full-repo pyright runs reliable.

## Proposal

Add manually dispatched RWX pipelines, `.rwx/pyright.yml` and `.rwx/pyrefly.yml`, that run pyright and pyrefly with a synced venv on the exact local git state, including uncommitted changes. Invoke it from the CLI:

```
rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait
rwx run .rwx/pyrefly.yml --wait
```

Why RWX instead of a Conductor setup script (`uv sync`):

- `rwx run` uploads a patch of local state (staged, unstaged and untracked files), so verification does not need a commit or push. See the [`rwx run` reference](https://www.rwx.com/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run).
- CI memory is not constrained like the sandbox.
- It uses the same pinned toolchain and cached `deps` task as `tests.yml` and `trunk-check.yml`, so local and CI results match.

## Investigation

- `.rwx/tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml` and `validate-assets.yml` already define a `cli:` trigger with `init.commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}`. They already run via `rwx run <file>`.
- They all clone with `git/clone` at `init.commit-sha`. `rwx run` layers the local patch on top of that clone. I haven't verified this end to end. See the open questions below.
- They share a checksum-pinned `uv-install` task and a `deps` task. `deps` runs `uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --group dev`, filtered to `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version` so it stays cached.
- `trunk-check.yml` already runs pyright through Trunk with `.venv`, but only as a diff-only lint (`--upstream`). It has no way to run pyright on a chosen set of files or on the whole project.
- `rwx dispatch` is a different mechanism. It launches a pre-configured workflow by key and takes `--param` and `--ref`, but no local patch. It is not suited to "verify my working tree".
- `pyrightconfig.json` extends `configs/pyrightconfig.json` (strict mode) with `venvPath: "."` and `venv: ".venv"`. The CI venv lives at `.venv`, so no config change is needed.
- `pyright` is run through Trunk (`.trunk/trunk.yaml`). Confirm whether it is also in the `dev` dependency group. If not, the pipeline needs either an added dev dependency or `uvx pyright` pinned to the Trunk version.

## Proposed design

`.rwx/pyright.yml` (and `.rwx/pyrefly.yml`, same structure):

- **Trigger:** `cli:` only, with no `github:` block. It is not a required status, so the merge queue is not affected (see the AGENTS.md note about path-filtered or non-reporting checks).
- **Tasks:** `code` (`git/clone`), `uv-install` and `deps`, copied from the existing files. Then a `pyright` task with `cache: false`, matching the other pipelines. Consider factoring out shared setup into one reusable definition, because it is now duplicated four times.
- **Targets:** an optional `init` parameter, for example `--init paths="app/foo.py app/bar.py"`, defaulting to the whole project. It lets an agent verify specific files quickly.
- **Rule filter:** optionally another `init` parameter that restricts output to one rule, for example `reportUnknownMemberType`.
- **Output:** use `--outputjson` and exit nonzero on errors, so `rwx run --wait --json` is usable by agents.

## Second pipeline: pyrefly

pyrefly is a separate checker that Trunk already runs (`pyrefly-plugin` v0.2.1 in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`). It needs its own pipeline, `.rwx/pyrefly.yml`, with the same `cli:` trigger and `code`, `uv-install` and `deps` tasks. Run it as `uv run pyrefly check`, which reads `pyrefly.toml` (`project-includes` covers `app`, `cli`, `components`, `scripts` and `tests`).

- `pyrefly.toml` sets `search-path = ["."]` and `python-interpreter-path = ".venv/bin/python"`. Both resolve relative to the config file, so they work in the RWX checkout once `deps` has created `.venv`.
- Keep pyrefly separate from pyright so each can be run, cached and failed independently, and so their results are not mixed.
- Confirm `pyrefly` is in the `dev` dependency group (it isn't visible in `pyproject.toml`). If it isn't, add it or pin `uvx pyrefly` to the version the Trunk plugin uses.
- Accept the same optional `paths` init parameter as the pyright pipeline.
- Because the two pipelines share setup, this strengthens the case for factoring the shared tasks out.

## Open questions

1. **Patch handling:** `git/clone` is given an explicit `ref`. Confirm that `rwx run` still applies the local patch in that case, and does not just check out the pushed sha. Before relying on this, test with an uncommitted edit that is known to fail pyright.
2. **Unpushed commits:** if HEAD has not been pushed, can the clone still resolve it? Document the push-first requirement if not.
3. **Scope:** should this one pipeline also run `trunk check` and `pytest` on demand, or stay pyright-only? `tests.yml` and `trunk-check.yml` already work with `rwx run` and could just be documented.
4. **Docs:** add the `rwx run` workflow to `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.entire/agent-guide.md`. Agents should reach for it when there is no `.venv`, instead of retrying locally.
5. **Local venv:** should we also add a Conductor `[scripts] setup = "uv sync --frozen"`, or is RWX the only supported verification path? Both can coexist. The setup script helps editing and quick tests; RWX covers heavy checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait` and `rwx run .rwx/pyrefly.yml --wait` each checks the local working tree, including uncommitted and untracked files, and fails on a deliberately introduced pyright error.
- [ ] The pipeline can be narrowed to specific files, and the narrowing is documented.
- [ ] The pipeline is not a required status and does not run on PRs or pushes.
- [ ] The workflow is documented where agents will find it.
- [ ] The `deps` task is cached across runs when the lockfile is unchanged.

## References

- #347: pragma removal that exposed the gap
- [`rwx run`](https://www.rwx.com/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run), [init parameters](https://www.rwx.com/docs/init-parameters), [CI reference workflow](https://rwx.com/docs/rwx/guides/ci)
- `.rwx/tests.yml`, `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, `.trunk/trunk.yaml` (pyright override), `pyrightconfig.json`

# On-demand pyright with a synced venv. Manual only: no github trigger, so it
# never runs on PRs or pushes and is not a required status.
#   rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait
#   rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait --init paths="app/foo.py app/bar.py"
# `rwx run` layers the local working tree (incl. uncommitted/untracked files)
# on the clone; HEAD must be pushed so `commit-sha` resolves.
on:
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      paths: ""

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}

  # Checksum-pinned uv installer: fails closed if the script at the versioned
  # URL ever changes. No packaged uv/install leaf exists in the RWX catalog.
  - key: uv-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # Filtered to the lockfile inputs so this stays cached across ordinary
  # commits. --no-install-project: sources are outside the filter; `uv run`
  # installs the project itself.
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install, code]
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock
      - .python-version
    run: uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --group dev

  # pyright is pinned to the Trunk version (not in the dev group). Installed in
  # its own task, with no dependency on `code`, so it is cached across runs
  # regardless of source changes. The version call also fetches the node runtime pyright needs, so that is cached too.
  - key: pyright-install
    use: uv-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      uv tool install pyright==1.1.414
      pyright --version

  - key: pyright
    use: [code, deps, pyright-install]
    cache: false
    env:
      CHECK_PATHS: ${{ init.paths }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
      pyright --pythonpath .venv/bin/python --project pyrightconfig.json ${CHECK_PATHS}

Base directory for this skill: /home/vercel-sandbox/buridan-ui/.claude/skills/rwx

# RWX CLI in this repo

CI definitions live in `.rwx/` (`tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml`, `validate-assets.yml`, `trunk-impacted-targets.yml`). Each has an `on.cli` trigger, so it can be started locally.

## Auth: two injected tokens, one per RWX workspace

Two env vars are injected into the environment, named `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_<SUFFIX>`. Each token is scoped to one RWX workspace. List the names without values:

```bash
env | grep -E '^RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_' | cut -d= -f1
```

The `<SUFFIX>` is the workspace name, uppercased. The token for this repo is the one whose suffix matches the repo owner (the owner in the `git remote` URL, e.g. `github.com/<owner>/buridan-ui`, uppercased). Use the other token only for runs in the other workspace.

The CLI reads only `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (or `--access-token`), so export the matching token under that name. Do this per command and never print the token:

```bash
OWNER=$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*[:/]([^/]+)/[^/]+(\.git)?$#\1#' | tr a-z A-Z)
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="REDACTED"RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER")"
# or, one-off:
rwx runs list --access-token "$RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

A run, task, or log ID only resolves under the workspace that owns it. If a lookup returns not-found or unauthorized, switch tokens.

## Running a pipeline with your current git changes

`rwx run` sends a git patch with the run, so no commit or push is needed:

- Base: the closest ancestor of local `HEAD` that is already on `origin`. `event.git.sha` resolves to it.
- Patch on top: unpushed local commits, staged changes, unstaged changes, and untracked files.
- Excluded: anything in `.gitignore`. Git LFS changes error out; commit and push those first.
- `RWX_DISABLE_GIT_PATCH=1` turns patching off.

```bash
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --wait --fail-fast          # run CI on the working tree, wait for result
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --target <task-key> --wait  # only one task (and its dependencies)
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --title "wip: my change" --json
```

The `git/clone` task takes `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}`, and the `cli` trigger sets `commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}`. That wiring is what makes the patch apply, so keep it when editing `.rwx/*.yml`. Edits to the `.rwx` files themselves are also picked up locally.

## Logs and results

```bash
rwx runs list
rwx results <run-id>                          # status and failures for a run
rwx logs <task-id>                            # download logs for a task
rwx logs <run-id> --task <task-key> --output /tmp/logs
```

`rwx run` prints the run URL and ID. Use `--json` for parsing.

## Docs

`rwx docs search "<query>"` and `rwx docs pull /docs/cli-triggers` (also `/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run`).

content.text:
Both pipelines work on the local working tree, including untracked files. I ran them on RWX and the results below are from those runs.

- **Auth:** the `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO` token that the rwx skill docs tell you to use doesn't exist. The environment injects it as `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO`, so I exported that value as `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`. The injected `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_MARCHILI` token fails with a 403.
- **Clean file:** `rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait --init paths="app/__init__.py"` succeeded.
- **Pyright on a bad file:** I created an untracked `app/zz_probe.py` containing `x: int = "a"`. The run failed with `app/zz_probe.py:1:10 - error: Type "Literal['a']" is not assignable to declared type "int"`. RWX reported "Included a git patch for uncommitted changes", so the local patch layers over the clone.
- **Pyrefly on the same file:** the run failed. I only checked that the run failed, not what pyrefly reported.
